findings.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:869 — P1, confidence 75; `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`: Removing the configured-host guard makes truncation apply to every embedded topic whenever the global flag is enabled, including instances with no allowed embedding host.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — P1, confidence 100; `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`: The feature has no verification that an administrator can create, edit, or delete a host-to-category relationship or that the selected category is used for imported embeddings.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — P1, confidence 100; `host = uri.host`: The lookup discards the URI port while persisted hosts retain validated ports, so a configured host such as `example.com:3000` can never match an embed URL and its category mapping is unusable.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — P1, confidence 100; `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`: Multiple rows can represent the same host because no uniqueness invariant exists, and this unordered first-row lookup can route embeds for that host to an arbitrary category.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — P2, confidence 100; `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`: Every public embed authorization/import performs a non-sargable `lower(host)` lookup with no matching functional index, producing a table scan on the request hot path as host mappings grow.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — P1, confidence 75; `t.integer :category_id, null: false`: The host-to-category relationship has no foreign-key or existence invariant, so deleted or invalid category IDs leave an allowed host whose imports no longer have a valid destination category.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — P1, confidence 100; `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`: A legacy host containing a quote is interpolated into executable SQL, allowing a pre-deploy setting editor to run arbitrary SQL with the migration connection's privileges.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — P1, confidence 100; `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`: This passes without invoking create, update, or destroy, so invalid params, persistence failures, and response regressions in the newly added CRUD controller remain undetected.

spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:6 — P1, confidence 100; `expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`: This passes without exercising show or update, so the new embedding serialization and host-loading behavior can fail in production while the added controller spec remains green.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:869 — P1, confidence 75; `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`: Removing the configured-host guard makes truncation apply to every embedded topic whenever the global flag is enabled, including instances with no allowed embedding host.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that removing the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check makes truncation apply to topics without allowed embedding hosts. However, looking at the diff, the old code was `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and the new code is `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The key point is that `has_topic_embed?` checks if the topic has an associated TopicEmbed record. TopicEmbed records are only created when content is imported via the embedding system, which now requires an EmbeddableHost record to exist (as shown in the new EmbeddableHost model and the changes to embed_controller.rb). So if there's no embeddable host configured, no TopicEmbed records would be created, and `has_topic_embed?` would return false. The behavior is functionally equivalent - topics can only have embeds if embedding is properly configured. This is not a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — P1, confidence 100; `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`: The feature has no verification that an administrator can create, edit, or delete a host-to-category relationship or that the selected category is used for imported embeddings.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes the test coverage as insufficient, noting that the spec only verifies inheritance rather than testing actual CRUD functionality. This is a test quality/coverage concern, not a bug or defect in the actual code. The diff shows working controller implementations (create, update, destroy actions in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb), model validations, and integration with TopicEmbed. The code itself appears functional - the finding is about test completeness, which is a style/quality nit rather than a real defect in the code being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — P1, confidence 100; `host = uri.host`: The lookup discards the URI port while persisted hosts retain validated ports, so a configured host such as `example.com:3000` can never match an embed URL and its category mapping is unusable.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in embeddable_host.rb: The validation regex on line 2 allows ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i`. The before_validation hook strips the protocol and path but preserves the port in the host field. However, in `record_for_host` method (lines 10-17), `uri.host` is used which returns only the hostname without the port (per URI standard behavior). So if a user configures 'example.com:3000' as an embeddable host, and a request comes from 'http://example.com:3000/page', `uri.host` returns 'example.com' (without port), but the database has 'example.com:3000'. The WHERE clause `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` would compare 'example.com' against 'example.com:3000' and fail to match. This is a real bug where hosts with ports would never match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — P1, confidence 100; `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`: Multiple rows can represent the same host because no uniqueness invariant exists, and this unordered first-row lookup can route embeds for that host to an arbitrary category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model has no unique constraint on the host column - the migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table with just `t.string :host, null: false` without any uniqueness constraint. The model validation in app/models/embeddable_host.rb only validates format, not uniqueness. The `record_for_host` method uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` which would return an arbitrary row if multiple records exist for the same host. This could lead to embeds being routed to different categories inconsistently. However, the severity is debatable - this is more of a data integrity issue that requires admin action to create duplicate hosts, and the practical impact depends on whether the admin UI prevents duplicates (which it doesn't appear to based on the controller code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — P2, confidence 100; `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`: Every public embed authorization/import performs a non-sargable `lower(host)` lookup with no matching functional index, producing a table scan on the request hot path as host mappings grow.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in app/models/embeddable_host.rb performs a case-insensitive lookup using `lower()` function on the host column. Looking at the migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the table is created with just a `host` column but no index is added. Without a functional index on `lower(host)`, this query will indeed perform a sequential table scan. However, this is a performance optimization concern rather than a correctness bug. The code will work correctly, just potentially slower as the table grows. For a typical embedding hosts table which would have very few rows (likely single digits to low hundreds at most), this is unlikely to be a significant performance issue in practice. While technically valid, this is more of an optimization suggestion than a critical defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — P1, confidence 75; `t.integer :category_id, null: false`: The host-to-category relationship has no foreign-key or existence invariant, so deleted or invalid category IDs leave an allowed host whose imports no longer have a valid destination category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out that category_id has `null: false` constraint but no foreign key constraint to the categories table. Looking at the diff, this is accurate - the migration creates the column without a foreign key reference. However, the EmbeddableHost model does have `belongs_to :category` and the controller code in save_host() sets a default: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`. The real issue is that if a category is deleted, the embeddable_host records pointing to it would have orphaned category_ids. This is a valid data integrity concern - there's no ON DELETE CASCADE or SET NULL, and no application-level protection against category deletion leaving invalid references. The TopicEmbed.import code uses `eh.try(:category_id)` which would pass an invalid category_id to PostCreator if the category was deleted. This is a real architectural/data integrity issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — P1, confidence 100; `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`: A legacy host containing a quote is interpolated into executable SQL, allowing a pre-deploy setting editor to run arbitrary SQL with the migration connection's privileges.

adjudication.rationale: The migration code at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert the host value directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."`. The variable `h` comes from parsing a site setting value that was previously stored by users. If a malicious admin had stored a host value containing SQL injection characters (like a single quote), this would allow arbitrary SQL execution during the migration. This is a real SQL injection vulnerability in the migration code, though the attack surface is limited to values that were previously stored in site settings by admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — P1, confidence 100; `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`: This passes without invoking create, update, or destroy, so invalid params, persistence failures, and response regressions in the newly added CRUD controller remain undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes the test file for only checking class inheritance rather than testing the actual CRUD operations. Looking at the diff, the test in spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only verifies that the controller is a subclass of AdminController. While this is a minimal test, this is a code review concern about test coverage/quality rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness problem in the actual code. The controller code itself in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb appears functional. The finding is essentially a suggestion to add more comprehensive tests, which is a style/coverage concern rather than a real defect in the code being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:6 — P1, confidence 100; `expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`: This passes without exercising show or update, so the new embedding serialization and host-loading behavior can fail in production while the added controller spec remains green.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes the test spec for only checking class inheritance rather than testing actual controller behavior. Looking at the diff, the test at spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb only verifies that Admin::EmbeddingController inherits from Admin::AdminController. While this is a minimal test, it's not a bug or defect in the code itself - it's a test coverage concern. The controller code itself (in app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb) is functional and correct. The finding is about test quality/coverage, not about a bug in the actual application code. This is more of a code review suggestion about test completeness rather than identifying a real defect that would cause production failures.
